title: Compact cross-platform builder and adaptive cache retention
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our CI fleet builds and test runners currently rely on >10 flavour-specific builder images (node, python, go, rust variants) with duplicated layers and differing toolchain versions. This increases image size, cache fragmentation, and makes cold builds and cross-platform builds slow and non-deterministic. We also keep cache entries indefinitely which increases storage costs and reduces cache hit quality.

Goal: Replace the heterogeneous builders with a compact cross-platform builder contract (single base + language-specific toolsets installed at build-time), introduce an adaptive cache retention policy (TTL + LRU heuristics based on recent frequency), and add cache-priming hooks for important release branches. This should reduce median CI wall time for cold builds, shrink pushed image sizes, and lower remote cache storage costs while keeping developer ergonomics intact.
acceptance_criteria: Single canonical builder base image (multi-arch) is published and referenced by >90% of build pipelines
Median cold CI build time reduced by >=30% for cross-language repos compared to baseline (measured across last 30 runs)
Remote cache storage growth rate reduced by >=40% month-over-month after adaptive retention rollout
Cache TTL heuristic exists and is configurable per-project; defaults applied to all repos
Rollback plan and compatibility layer in place for pipelines that need legacy toolchain versions
Documentation and migration guide published in Confluence and linked from template repos
tasks: Design builder contract (OS, shell, package manager expectations) and publish spec
Assemble compact base image (musl-compatible slim OS + glibc shim where required) and build multi-arch manifests
Create language toolset installers that run at build-time to avoid per-language base images
Implement adaptive cache retention service (TTL + frequency scoring) in cache proxy
Add cache-priming workflow for release branch builds and nightly priming jobs
Update CI templates to reference new builder and add opt-out flag for legacy builds
Run staged rollout across 10 pilot repos, collect metrics, iterate before org-wide rollout
Add cost and performance dashboards in Console to track changes
comments: 2026-03-05 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after retro — CI team flagged storage costs and several flaky cold builds. Initial spike shows duplicated layers across node/python/go images totaling ~4.8GB per builder on average.
2026-03-07 Marco Reyes: Drafted builder contract and shared in #infra-ci. Feedback from platform eng: ensure /workspace mount semantics unchanged and preserve s6-init behavior for service containers.
2026-03-09 Design review: UX/DevX requested minimal changes to developer local experience. Agreed to ship a thin shim that allows local 'rfw build' to reproduce CI installs.

2026-03-10 PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/compact-builder (WIP) — includes Dockerfile, multi-arch manifest generation, and smoke tests. @sre requested alt qemu runners for arm validation.
2026-03-12 Marco Reyes: Implemented cache retention prototype in cache-proxy v0.3. Added metrics (hit_rate, eviction_rate, TTL_distribution). Running canary against staging cache.
2026-03-13 QA: Flaky test discovered in go-toolset installer on arm64 (locale/openssl mismatch). Added follow-up task to pin openssl and add locale fallback.
2026-03-14 Aisha Kapoor: Runbook and rollback plan added. Rollout plan: pilot -> 25 repos (1 week) -> 100 repos (2 weeks) -> org-wide. If >5% failure rate in pilot, pause and revert template change.
